<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- search: Search the web via the local SearXNG instance (titles, URLs, snippets)
- fetch: Fetch a specific http/https URL directly and return its text content (HTML → plain text)

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use search to look up current web information or documentation.
- Use search with max_results when fewer or more results are needed (max 10).
- Use search with freshness to look only for recent results (day, week, month, year), category to restrict the result type (e.g. it, news, images), language to pin the result language (e.g. de, en), and page (1–10) to paginate beyond the first result page.
- If a filtered search returns no results, retry with fewer filters: on this container, freshness only applies to a small set of engines per category (e.g. 'it' covers only hackernews, 'news' just two), so 0 results can mean that engine set simply had no hits — broaden the category or drop freshness.
- Use fetch to read the text content of a specific page URL.
- Use fetch with max_chars to limit output length for long pages (hard cap 20000).
- Use fetch with offset to continue reading a long page (the next offset is given in the truncation notice), and raw=true to get the unmodified body without HTML→text conversion (e.g. JSON APIs).
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

<project_instructions path="/home/julian/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md">
# Global instructions
As soon as your task is to programm something allways prioritize Test Driven Development (TDD) than do so.
Prefer simple, robust and performant solutions and check if something can get broken before making changes. Make sure to test against breaking changes.
Allways start your answer with a short abstract of what you want to say. After that you can write down your full response.
The last part every answer has to include is instructions for the user and what he has to do next. If there is nothing to do also tell the user.
Allways stick to english as our primary communication language.
Whenever you think you read something interesting about the user you can persist this knowledge into `~/.pi/agent/USER.md` so you can evolve into an even better assistant.

<!-- pi-env:start (managed by setup-pi-tools.sh) -->
## Safety rules (all projects)
- Git: use only read-only git commands (status, diff, log, show, ls-files, rev-parse, blame). Never run `git init` or any other git command that changes or creates a repository, unless I ask for that exact command in my own message. A "yes" to another question is not such a request.
- Never delete directories recursively (`rm -r`, `rm -rf`) and never overwrite files outside the scope of the current task without asking me first.
- If a command is blocked by the confirmation-dialog extension or declined by me, do not retry it in another form (no `sh -c`, aliases, scripts, or full paths). Continue without it, or ask me to run it myself.
- Never create `.pi/` files or scan the whole directory when running directly in my home directory; ask which project directory is meant.

## Planning and memory
- When a task should be planned before it is executed (new feature, workflow change, larger bug), use the `plan` skill.
- If the project has `.pi/LOG.md`: after a compaction or at the start of a session, read `.pi/PLAN.md` and `tail -n 60 .pi/LOG.md` before doing anything else.

## CLI tools (call them via bash)
- `rg` (ripgrep): search code and text. Use `-n`, single-quoted patterns, `-M 200`; `-l` for file names only, `-F` for literal text, `-w` for whole words, `-U` for patterns spanning several lines. `rg --files -g '*name*'` finds files by name.
- `ctags -x --sort=no <file>`: outline of a file (functions, classes, methods with line numbers). Always use `-x`; without it ctags writes a `tags` file.
- `jq '<filter>' <file.json>`: query JSON (e.g. `jq '.scripts' package.json`) instead of reading the whole file.
- Read files with `read` and `offset`/`limit` instead of `cat`; check the length with `wc -l` first. Keep command output small (`| head -50`).
<!-- pi-env:end -->

</project_instructions>

### New Features

 - Fork sessions whose folder is gone: when a session's original folder was moved or deleted, you can now fork it into the
   current folder instead of only continuing, so later resumes no longer ask. See Continue or switch sessions
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.2/packages/coding-agent/docs/sessions.md#continue-or-switch-sessions).

 ### Changed

 - When a session's working directory no longer exists, for example after the project folder was renamed, interactive mode now
   offers Continue, Fork, or Cancel instead of only continuing. Continue runs the session in the current directory without
   storing the choice, as before; Fork copies it into the current directory as a new session with a new ID, like --fork, so the
   next resume no longer asks. This applies at startup (--session, --resume), to /resume, to /import, and to ctx.switchSession()
   from extensions (#11975 (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11975) by @petrroll (https://github.com/petrroll), fixes
   #11060 (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11060))

 ### Fixed

 - Fixed /import of a session whose working directory no longer exists leaving a copy in the session directory, and continuing it
   leaving a second copy with the same ID (s.jsonl and s-1.jsonl); the failed copy is now removed (#11975
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11975) by @petrroll (https://github.com/petrroll), fixes #11060
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11060))
 - Fixed Anthropic OAuth requests reporting an outdated Claude Code version

 [1.5.1] - 2026-11-09

 ### New Features

 - Shell login and logout: use pi auth login <provider> and pi auth logout <provider> without starting a session, with API-key
   and no-browser sign-in options. See Credential commands
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md#credential-commands).
 - Idle prompt cache warming: eligible caches now stay warm for up to 30 minutes between runs when a refresh is expected to pay
   for itself. See cacheWarming
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md#model-and-thinking).
 - Anthropic message threads: requests send only new messages while the server continues the conversation, with full-request
   fallback when earlier context changes. See Anthropic compatibility
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/models-configuration.md#anthropic-messages).
 - Richer Mermaid diagrams: pie charts, author-defined styles, clickable labels on supported terminals, and diagrams in expanded
   branch and compaction summaries. See Display settings
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md#terminal-and-display) and Markdown
   transformers
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md#piregistermarkdowntransformertransf
   ormer-options).
 - GitHub Copilot classifiers: call Microsoft-Decision-1 through codemode models.classify() for typed decisions and
   probabilities. See Use classifier models
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/models.md#use-classifier-models).
 - Package update summaries: pi update --extensions reports each package's npm version or git commit change and distinguishes
   unchanged, skipped, and warned updates. See Update Pi or packages
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md#update-pi-or-packages).

 ### Breaking Changes

 - Custom GrepOperations.readFile callbacks are no longer called for context lines. The field remains accepted as optional and
   deprecated so existing integrations still compile. The grep tool now takes context lines from ripgrep and no longer reads
   matched files itself. To search a remote system, override grep's execute(); see Remote Execution
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md#remote-execution) (#9276
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9276))
 - OpenAI-compatible models no longer send "tools": [] when all tools are disabled in a session that has used tools; the field is
   omitted. This fixes 400 errors (tools must not be an empty array) from vLLM 0.20+, also behind LiteLLM. If your proxy requires
   tools once the history has tool calls, such as older LiteLLM versions in front of Anthropic, set
   compat.requiresToolsWithToolHistory: true for that model in models.json (#11843
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11843))

 ### Added

 - pi update now lists each updated package with its npm version or git commit change, for example npm:foo 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0, and
   prints Packages are already up to date when nothing changed. When nothing changed but an update printed a warning, for example
   because npm left the old version installed after resolving stale registry metadata, it prints No packages were updated, see
   the warnings above instead; in offline mode it prints Skipped package updates (offline mode). PackageManager.update() reports
   each changed package as a new result progress event whose message holds that line (#11707
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11707), #11711 (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11711))
 - Anthropic sessions now use message threads: each request sends only the new messages and the server continues from the
   previous reply, falling back to the full request when the conversation changed (for example after compaction or a tool list
   change). On by default for the anthropic provider on api.anthropic.com; set compat.supportsMessageThreads in models.json to
   enable it for gateways that forward the thread field, or to turn it off. Cache warming does not touch the session's thread
   (#11545 (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11545))
 - pi.registerMarkdownTransformer() takes an optional { messageTypes } that selects the Markdown surfaces a transformer runs on.
   Besides user, assistant, and thinking Markdown, transformers can now opt into custom (custom messages and skill blocks),
   summary (branch and compaction summaries), and changelog (What's New, /changelog, the Extension Updates notice, and the Update
   Available note). Without options a transformer runs on user, assistant, and thinking Markdown as before. The built-in Mermaid
   renderer now also draws diagrams in expanded branch and compaction summaries
 - pi auth login <provider> logs in to a provider from the shell without starting a session, for example pi auth login radius. It
   signs in with an account in the browser and exits; --api-key saves an API key instead, and --no-browser uses device code or
   copy-code sign-in instead. Logging in to Radius also configures the Radius MCP server. pi auth logout <provider> removes the
   stored credentials, like /logout
 - ctx.ui.custom() overlays now honor the blocked option: pi reports blocked program status (OSC 7501) from when the overlay is
   shown until it calls done(), also while it is hidden with setHidden(). Closing one overlay keeps other open questions blocked
   (#11816 (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11816))
 - Added the qwen-token-plan-individual-cn provider for Qwen Token Plan Individual on the China endpoint, using
   QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_CN_API_KEY (#7989 (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/7989) by @bigoldcat123
   (https://github.com/bigoldcat123))
 - Added Microsoft-Decision-1 classifier support through GitHub Copilot, including codemode models.classify() (#11679
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11679) by @Marvae (https://github.com/Marvae))
 - Added compat.promptCacheKeyMode ("auto", "enabled", or "disabled") to enable prompt cache keys for compatible proxies or omit
   them for endpoints that reject them. Set it in models.json when using pi (#9442
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9442) by @dannote (https://github.com/dannote))
 - Added compat.requiresNonNullAssistantContent for OpenAI-compatible endpoints that require an empty string instead of null in
   assistant messages containing only tool calls. Set it in models.json when using pi (#8118
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8118) by @gaoyk19 (https://github.com/gaoyk19))
 - Added syntax highlighting for Dart, Nix, Groovy, and Gradle files in read and write views (#11643
   (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11643))
 - Added GLM 5.3 to the Qwen Token Plan Individual model allowlist (#11658 (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11658))
 - Added Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2) to the anthropic provider ($8/$40 per million input/output tokens, 1M context, 128K
   output). Like Fable 5.1 it uses per-message effort and mid-conversation system messages; requests its safety classifiers
   refuse before any output are answered by Claude Opus 5 through server-side fallback and billed at Opus 5's price. Claude Fable
   5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on other providers, such as OpenRouter's `anthropic/claude-fable-5.2`, get the same per-message effort
   support

# Skill: Quiet Verifier (Token-Safe Testing & Verification)

Running an unfiltered `npm test`, `pytest`, or `cargo test` command on a large codebase can dump 30,000+ tokens of console logs into your context window, immediately triggering a destructive auto-compaction. Follow these rules for EVERY verification command.

## 1. The 3 Iron Laws of Verification
1. **Scope to Single Files:** Never run the entire repository test suite during iterative coding. Always pass the specific test file or test name matching the module you edited.
2. **Use Quiet & Fail-Fast Flags:** Always pass flags that suppress passing test chatter and abort after the first 1–3 failures (`--bail`, `-x`, `-q`).
3. **Mandatory Output Piping:** Every build, test, typecheck, or linter command executed via `bash` **MUST** end with `2>&1 | head -n 60` or `2>&1 | tail -n 60`.

## 2. Standard Quiet Command Patterns by Stack

*(Always check `.pi/PROJECT_MAP.md` first for project-specific commands; otherwise use these patterns)*

### TypeScript / JavaScript (Node, Vitest, Jest, Playwright)
- **TypeScript Typecheck (first 50 error lines only):**
  ~~~bash
  npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false 2>&1 | head -n 50
  ~~~
- **Vitest (single file, dot reporter, bail on first error):**
  ~~~bash
  npx vitest run path/to/file.test.ts --reporter=dot --bail=1 2>&1 | tail -n 60
  ~~~
- **Jest (single file, silent console, bail):**
  ~~~bash
  npx jest path/to/file.test.ts --silent --bail 2>&1 | tail -n 60
  ~~~
- **ESLint / Biome (single file, quiet/errors only):**
  ~~~bash
  npx eslint path/to/file.ts --quiet 2>&1 | head -n 50
  ~~~

### Python (Pytest, Ruff, Mypy)
- **Pytest (single file, stop on first failure, short traceback):**
  ~~~bash
  pytest path/to/test_file.py -q -x --tb=short --no-header 2>&1 | tail -n 60
  ~~~
- **Ruff & Mypy (targeted check):**
  ~~~bash
  ruff check path/to/file.py --quiet 2>&1 | head -n 50
  mypy path/to/file.py --no-error-summary 2>&1 | head -n 50
  ~~~

### Rust / Go / .NET (C#)
- **Rust (`cargo`):**
  ~~~bash
  cargo check --message-format=short 2>&1 | head -n 60
  cargo test test_name -- --quiet 2>&1 | tail -n 60
  ~~~
- **Go:**
  ~~~bash
  go test -run TestName ./path/to/pkg 2>&1 | tail -n 60
  ~~~
- **C# (.NET):**
  ~~~bash
  dotnet build --no-restore -v q /clp:ErrorsOnly 2>&1 | head -n 60
  dotnet test --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TestName" -v q 2>&1 | tail -n 60
  ~~~

- Extensions: `~/.pi/agent/extensions/*.ts`
- Releases: `~/.pi/agent/install/releases/<ver>/node_modules/@earendil-works/{pi-coding-agent,pi-tui}`

### 1. Identify old and new versions


### 3. Audit extensions against the changed APIs

```bash

rg -n "<api1>|<api2>|..." -o | head -30          # only changed APIs from step 2
```

For every hit, open the matched lines and distinguish **pi API usage** from **local implementations with the same name** (e.g. a local `classify()` function is not `models.classify()`). Report each hit as affected / not-affected with a reason.

### 4. Verify imported symbols exist in the new types

### 5. Runtime load test (authoritative)

```bash
node ~/.pi/agent/bin/pi-ext-loadtest.mjs          # auto-detects active release
```

It imports every extension through jiti with the same alias map pi's loader uses. Expect `ALL LOADED`, exit 0. This catches import-time breakage; it does **not** check types — step 6 does.

### 6. Typecheck against the new types (and classify errors)

# Pi extension upgrade check

After a pi update, prove that the extensions in `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` are unaffected instead of assuming it. pi loads extensions through jiti with **aliases that point into the active release** (`~/.pi/agent/install/releases/<ver>/node_modules/@earendil-works/...`), so type errors never break loading — you must check *both* runtime loading and type compatibility.

Key paths (agent dir = `~/.pi/agent`, override via `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`):

- Extensions: `~/.pi/agent/extensions/*.ts`
- Releases: `~/.pi/agent/install/releases/<ver>/node_modules/@earendil-works/{pi-coding-agent,pi-tui}`
- Load test: `~/.pi/agent/bin/pi-ext-loadtest.mjs [version]`
- Editor symlinks: `~/.pi/agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/*` (symlinks into one release; must be re-pointed after an update)
- Extension project suites, if any: `~/.pi/agent/projects/<name>` (e.g. themes has `npm test`)

## Workflow

Run every step; keep command output small (`| head -n 30` / `| tail -n 5`).

### 1. Identify old and new versions

```bash
ls ~/.pi/agent/install/releases/        # all installed versions
pi --version                            # active one
```

### 2. List changed APIs from the changelog

Read the changelog section old→new (GitHub `CHANGELOG.md` or the pasted notes). Extract: **breaking changes** and everything touching extension APIs — `GrepOperations`, `registerMarkdownTransformer`, `ctx.switchSession`, `ctx.ui.custom`/`blocked`, `models.classify`, `defineTool`/tool result types, `Component`/pi-tui classes, `pi auth`, `compat.*` model settings.

### 3. Audit extensions against the changed APIs

```bash
cd ~/.pi/agent/extensions
rg -n "<api1>|<api2>|..." -o | head -30          # only changed APIs from step 2
```

For every hit, open the matched lines and distinguish **pi API usage** from **local implementations with the same name** (e.g. a local `classify()` function is not `models.classify()`). Report each hit as affected / not-affected with a reason.

### 4. Verify imported symbols exist in the new types

Collect every symbol imported from `@earendil-works/pi-*` (`rg -o 'from "@earendil-works/[^"]+"' -N`), then confirm each name appears in the new release's `.d.ts` files. A missing symbol = extension broken.

### 5. Runtime load test (authoritative)

```bash
node ~/.pi/agent/bin/pi-ext-loadtest.mjs          # auto-detects active release
```

It imports every extension through jiti with the same alias map pi's loader uses. Expect `ALL LOADED`, exit 0. This catches import-time breakage; it does **not** check types — step 6 does.

### 6. Typecheck against the new types (and classify errors)

Create `/tmp/ext-tsconfig-<ver>.json` (one per pi version compared), with `paths` mapping both packages to that release's entry types. tsc does **not** expand `~` — substitute the real `$HOME` when writing the file:

```json
    "paths": {
      "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": ["install/releases/<ver>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/index.d.ts"],
      "@earendil-works/pi-tui": ["install/releases/<ver>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/index.d.ts"]
    }
  },

```

- **Errors** → repeat against the **old** release's types and `diff` the error sets (normalize: `grep -E '^[^(]+\.ts' | sort`). Errors present in **both** are pre-existing (jiti strips types, so they are inert); only **new** errors are caused by the upgrade. ### 7. Re-point the editor symlinks


`rm` only removes the link — it never touches the release directory. Only act while `[ -L ]` is true.

Table with: version pair, each changed API vs. extensions (affected/not), load test result, typecheck results (new vs pre-existing error counts), symlink state, test-suite results.
